intent: A first that happened at the far end of the map: the American flag-ball thinks while a pin lands on the hospital, the real 1968 portrait of the surgeon rises out of the country, a THEN/NOW split puts 18 days against decades of survival, and a counter runs the yearly transplants into the thousands.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country did the FIRST human heart transplant?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country did the first human heart transplant?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: United States, Britain, or South Africa?
South Africa. A Cape Town hospital, December 1967.

lines.direction: push toward the Cape; the US flag-ball thinks on 'American' with a dog sticker; the real 1968 portrait rises out of the country on 'Barnard'; the hospital pin and tag land on 'here' with a hospital sticker as the country pulses; portrait leaves at the end
lines.text: American teams had practised on hundreds of dogs. But Christiaan Barnard went first, on a Sunday morning here.

lines.direction: ease back a touch; the THEN/NOW split slides in on 'patient' — 18 days against 12+ years; a calendar sticker on 'patient', a sparkle on 'years' as the country pulses; split leaves at the end
lines.text: His patient lived 18 days. Today, half of all recipients live more than 12 years.

lines.direction: tighten on the Cape; the counter runs to 6,000 from 'hearts' to 'worldwide' with a heart sticker; a surgeon sticker on 'theatre' as the South African flag-ball grins and the country pulses; pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Around 6,000 hearts are now transplanted every year, worldwide. It all started in this operating theatre.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A first from the far end of the map. Follow us.
